headline: Accounting Close Lead
description_text:
TL;DR: We're looking for someone who has run a US GAAP close, sat across the table from Big 4 auditors, and wants to build a continuous close where AI does the routine work and people do the thinking. You'll own our month-end close and consolidation process across the US, Sweden and the UK, reporting to our Accounting Controller. You'll build a close designed for scale, with the structure and controls a much bigger company will need built in from the start rather than bolted on later. This is an operating role, not an advisory one.



Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.



The role

Most accounting teams take the close they have today and add AI to it. We'd rather design it from scratch, assuming agents and automation are available, and keep people for review, judgment and the hard calls. Over time we want the close to run continuously rather than as a scramble at month-end.

That only works if the structure underneath is solid. Every automated reconciliation still needs an owner, a review and evidence an auditor can rely on. Every journal entry an agent prepares still needs the right controls around it. You'll be the person who holds both ideas at once: pushing hard on automation while making sure what we build would hold up under SOX.

You'll report to our Accounting Controller, and work alongside a small team. This is a hands-on lead role. You'll own the close, do a lot of the work yourself and help build a legacy with no formal direct reports today.



What you’ll do

 - Own our month-end close and consolidation process across our US, Swedish and UK entities under US GAAP.

 - Run the close calendar so it lands on time every month, and shorten it as automation takes over routine work.

 - Partner with the Controller on the move toward a continuous close. Build or direct automated reconciliations, flux analysis and journal entry workflows, and decide where human review actually adds value.

 - Design controls, review steps and evidence trails into those workflows from the start, so they're audit-ready without a separate clean-up exercise.

 - Support the group external audit for your areas: PBC requests, walkthroughs, reconciliations and support for audit adjustments.

 - Assist with the preparation and support of statutory audits in the UK and Sweden.

 - Keep close documentation and policies current and clear enough that a new team member or an auditor can follow them.

 - Work with Order-to-Cash, Financial Systems, Data and FP&A so the GL, subledgers and source systems tie out and stay that way.

 - Coach the accountants on the team and raise the bar on quality and ownership.



What we’re looking for

 - Must have
   
   - Has personally run a month-end close and consolidation under US GAAP across multiple entities. You know where a close actually breaks.
   
   - Has been through Big 4 audits from the company side.
   
   - A real drive to build an AI-first, continuous close, with examples of close processes you've already automated or redesigned.
   
   - A deep respect for the rigor a public company needs: controls, review evidence, documentation and calendars that hold up under scrutiny. You see automation as a way to get more discipline with less effort, not a reason to skip it.
   
   - Operationally minded: you'd rather fix a broken process than write a memo about it.
   
   Nice to have
   
   - Has been through a company's journey from startup to IPO or public-company readiness, including SOX.
   
   - Big 4 audit background before moving in-house.
   
   - Experience with Swedish or UK statutory reporting and audits.
   
   - Hands-on experience with modern finance tooling (we use Light ERP and Lovable), and comfortable building your own automations.
   
   This role isn't for you if 
   
   - You want an established close to run rather than one to redesign.
   
   - You'd rather wait for the perfect tool than build a working solution yourself this week.
   
   - You'd automate a process without being able to explain to an auditor how it's controlled.
   
   - You see AI as a side project rather than the default way the work gets done.

headline: Head of Technical Accounting & Reporting
description_text:
TL;DR: We're looking for someone to own technical accounting and reporting at Lovable as we build toward being a generational company. You'll report to our Group Financial Controller. This is a builder's role: there is a lot to set up, and you'll do much of it yourself.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.



The role

Lovable's business model raises real accounting questions. We sell subscriptions and usage-based credits to millions of self-serve users and to enterprise customers, through our own billing, app stores and payment processors. We buy a lot of AI compute. We have US, Swedish and UK entities and we report under US GAAP. Most of these questions have been answered at a point in time. They need proper answers, written down, and kept current as the business changes, without slowing the business down to get there.

You'll own that. Stock-based compensation, leases, LLM commitments, consolidation and foreign currency, M&A accounting and whatever comes next as we launch new products and features. You'll own the accounting policies, the position papers and the relationship with our auditors on technical matters.

You'll also own external reporting: building the financial statements, disclosures and reporting calendar we'll need as a public company, well before we need them, and doing it in a way that is as automated as possible. We expect you to leverage AI to draft disclosures, tie out numbers and flag changes. You'll decide where that's safe and where a person has to own the judgment.

You'll report to our Group Financial Controller, and work closely with our head of Revenue Accounting and our Chief Accounting Officer, on the significant judgments.



What we’re looking for

Must have

 - Deep US GAAP expertise, with ASC 842 for leases and ASC 718 for Stock Based Compensation as a strength. You've written position papers that auditors have accepted on complex matters.

 - Big 4 background, ideally including exposure to national office, accounting advisory or SEC reporting work, followed by in-house experience at a technology company.

 - Has built or materially upgraded an external reporting process: financial statements, disclosures, tie-outs and the calendar behind them.

 - Can explain a complex accounting conclusion to an engineer or a product manager in plain English, and change their mind when the facts warrant it.

 - Comfortable operating in ambiguity and building an AI first function from the ground up.

 - Pragmatic about applying accounting guidance to minimize operational overhead.

Nice to have

 - Has operated in a hypergrowth environment, including ideally through an IPO or the first year as a public company, ie. S-1 or 10-K preparation and SOX implementation.

 - Experience with AI, cloud or consumption-based business models and their revenue and cost accounting.

 - Experience with IFRS and Swedish or UK statutory reporting.

 - Has leveraged AI tools to draft disclosures, research guidance or automate tie-outs, and has views on where they help and where they're dangerous.

This role isn't for you if

 - You want a team and an established process on day one.

 - You prefer to be asked for an opinion rather than go and find the questions yourself.

 - You'd rather write a perfect memo in 2 weeks than a good answer in two hours.

 - You see AI as a threat to technical accounting rather than a tool for doing it better.



What you’ll do

 - Own technical accounting at Lovable: research the questions, reach a defensible US GAAP conclusion, and write position papers that hold up with auditors.

 - Own technical accounting for AI compute and cost of revenue, stock-based compensation, leases, consolidation and foreign currency, and any new areas as they arise.

 - Write and maintain the accounting policy manual, and make sure the close team is applying it consistently.

 - Build the external reporting function: US GAAP consolidated financial statements, footnote disclosures, a reporting calendar and tie-out process that would meet public-company standards.

 - Own local statutory accounting and reporting for our Swedish and UK entities, ensuring the books comply with Swedish GAAP (K3) and UK GAAP (FRS 102), including local GAAP adjustments, statutory financial statements and reconciliations to US GAAP.

 - Collaborate with the wider accounting team reviewing the month-end close figures to ensure any adjustments are identified promptly and remediation measures put in place.

 - Be the point person coordinating the external audit: present significant judgments, new standards, complex transactions and prepare future audit committee-facing materials.

 - Assess new accounting standards and SEC requirements and plan our adoption.

 - Leverage AI tooling to draft, tie out and review, and set the standard for where human judgment is required.

 - Drive public-company readiness across accounting and reporting, including disclosure controls and SOX requirements.

headline: Corporate Communications & Public Affairs (Europe)

Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions.

Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward.

You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement.

You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom.

You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work.

You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you.




WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative.

We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it.

We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early.

Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.

description_text:

 - You already write with AI: for research, drafting and checking, not just polish. You know what it gets wrong and you catch it.

 - You test what you document. You'd rather try the feature and read the source than take someone's word for it, and when something's broken or confusing, you say so.

 - You're at home in docs-as-code: Git, Markdown and pull requests.

 - You ask engineers and PMs specific questions, and when documenting a feature shows it won't make sense to users, you raise it early, with reasons.

   - You've written for AI readers, or you're curious about it. 
   
   - You have UX writing or content design experience, or an interest in it. 
   
   - You can read code well enough to check how a feature actually behaves; writing code is not required.

What you'll do

 - Drive, don't wait. Features land every day, and bigger launches several times a month. You find out what's shipping before anyone tells you, and the docs are ready the day it ships.

 - Own it end to end. Work a feature out from the code and the product, write the page, verify it in Lovable, ship it, and keep it true as the product moves.

 - Care about the reader more than the feature. Our docs come with data: what people can't find, what the assistant couldn't answer, what support hears. You use it to decide what to write next.

 - Make the product better, not just explain it. Documenting a feature means using it end to end. You'll find the confusing label or the broken step and get it fixed before launch.

 - Write for three readers on one page. The non-technical builder, the developer, and the AI agent working on their behalf.

 - Build something that outlasts the week. AI drafts a lot of our pages. The human work is judgement: what a feature needs, what the engineer didn't mention, and the checks that keep hundreds of pages correct.

 - Where you'll start:
   
   - Enterprise. Identity and access, governance, audit, data residency: the pages a security team reads before they sign.
   
   - The developer surface. Take our API and MCP references from correct to complete.

 - An infrastructure engineer who has built and run data systems in production at scale, and wants the harder version of the problem: millions of tiny tenants on shared infrastructure.

 - Deep experience in at least one layer (ingestion, storage formats and table layout, query execution, or orchestration), and the range to work across the others.

 - Experience with multi-tenant or untrusted workloads: isolation, noisy neighbours, and keeping cost per tenant low.

 - Expose data, metadata and tools to the Lovable agent so it can build software on customers' data.

 - Run what you build, including observability, freshness and recovery.
   
   

The tech stack

We're building with tools that both humans and AI love:

 - Languages: Go, Rust, Python, SQL

 - Data: ClickHouse, BigQuery, Parquet on object storage

 - Streaming & orchestration: Pub/Sub, Temporal

 - Cloud: GCP, Cloudflare, AWS

headline: Internal Communications Lead
description_text:

This is a strategic operating role at the center of the company, reporting to the Head of Comms with a dotted line to our Cofounder and CEO. Your core job is making sure company leadership communication is clear, consistent, and compounding week after week as we scale. Around that core, you'll own the narrative, the moments, and the rhythms that keep a fast-growing global team aligned, and you'll run the programming lean, with AI doing the production work so your judgment goes where it matters most.



The challenge: when a company doubles in a year across offices and oceans, shared context is the first thing that can break. The warmth of a small team gets diluted by process. Your job is to make sure none of that happens: that every person at Lovable knows where we're going, why, and their part in it, and hears it in a voice that still feels like us.

Be the CEO's communications partner. You'll help make sure what the company hears is consistent from week to week and compounds over quarters. And you'll be a genuine advisor: in the room early, pressure-testing how a decision will land before it's made, and holding a mirror up to leadership when the message and the reality drift apart.



Own the company narrative and operating rhythm. You'll own recurring communications and the strategy behind them: the cadences that ensure every employee understands the strategy, the priorities, and the reasoning, not just the announcements. You'll connect the internal story to the external one so employees hear one narrative, whether it comes from the CEO, their manager, or the press.



Run the moments that matter. Fundraises, strategy rollouts, reorgs and leadership changes, and other high-stakes comms. You'll partner with the Office of the CEO and leadership team to make sure these moments are planned, humane, and land without whiplash: employees hear things that affect them before any rumor mill does.



Make our flagship forums worth showing up for. You'll own the editorial arc of company-wide all-hands, elevate the craft of everyone presenting, and keep these moments warm and personal as we grow past the size where that happens by default.



Build an AI-native internal comms engine. You'll run programming that would traditionally take a team, alone, by defaulting to AI and Lovable itself for input gathering, chasing, aggregating, drafting, and measurement. Human judgment stays where it belongs: editorial calls, sensitive moments, and final approval. If you're still doing production work manually after three months, something has gone wrong.



Raise the bar for how leaders communicate. At Lovable, functions own their own communication; internal comms is not a gatekeeper or a wordsmithing service. Your job is to make every leader and manager a better communicator: standards, tools, coaching, and talking points that equip managers to answer their teams' questions, because managers are the most trusted source most employees have.



Measure understanding, not reach. You'll build lightweight feedback loops that test whether messages actually landed: can people explain the strategy in their own words, do they feel informed, are the whispers going quiet. You write exceptionally. You know the difference between writing that informs and writing that aligns, and you can do both under deadline.



You're AI-native to your core. You instinctively reach for AI to do the gathering and aggregating, and you're excited to build internal tools on Lovable itself. You see leverage where others see headcount requests.



You read organizations well. You have a feel for the pulse of a company: what people are worried about, where context is missing, which message will land and which will breed cynicism. You listen as much as you broadcast, and you navigate cultural differences across our European and US offices with ease.



You're discreet, low-ego, and steady. You'll sit closer to sensitive information than almost anyone in the company. You handle it with care, you share credit reflexively, and you stay calm when plans change on a Tuesday afternoon.




WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
